title: Ops Resilience: Never Again
description: Power is restored. The PM wants answers: who did this, how did they do it, and what stops it happening again? DIS has one week to brief Parliament.
storyContext: Power is back. Most people will never know how close it got. But the PM knows, and Parliament wants answers. Your team has one week to explain who did this, how they got in, and what stops it from ever happening again. Your evidence will shape national cybersecurity policy for the next decade.

software-engineer.title: Design the Permanent Defence
software-engineer.instruction: The attack exploited a gap between the power station systems and the office network. Leadership wants a permanent fix. What do you propose?
software-engineer.hint: The best long-term defence closes the gap without creating new problems — like making it impossible to manage systems when you need to.

options.label: Every connection between stations and office networks must prove it's legitimate before being allowed through. Nothing trusted by default. Gold standard, but takes 18 months to roll out.
AI-powered security centre that watches everything around the clock, flags suspicious activity, and auto-responds to known threats. Operational in 3 months.
Physically cut all internet connections to critical systems forever. Ultimate defence, but every update needs an engineer on-site. No remote management.
Regional programme where neighbouring countries' utilities share attack details in real time. One country detecting an attack means everyone is warned instantly.

data-scientist.title: Build the Evidence Case
data-scientist.instruction: Intelligence suggests a state-backed attacker but the PM needs solid evidence for Parliament. Arrange the investigation steps.
data-scientist.hint: Gather all evidence before drawing conclusions. Build from concrete facts toward the bigger picture, and always be honest about how certain you are.

items.label: Compare the attacker's methods against a database of known groups
Trace network traffic backwards through disguised relay points to find the source
Study the malicious code for stylistic clues — like analysing handwriting
Check when attacks happened against working hours and time zones of suspected groups
Combine all evidence into a clear statement for Parliament with an honest confidence level

cloud-engineer.title: Design the Defence Architecture
cloud-engineer.instruction: Design an infrastructure that survives future attacks. Layer 1: stops attacks. Layers 2-3: detect and respond. Layer 4: recovers when things go wrong.
cloud-engineer.hint: Think about each tool's job — stopping, spotting, reacting, or recovering. Match each to the layer that fits its purpose.

items.label: Traffic Filter — blocks suspicious incoming traffic at the gate
Threat Detector — monitors and flags suspicious events
Auto-Responder — automatically acts on confirmed threats
Backup Control Centre — takes over if the main site goes down
Weakness Finder — scans for security gaps before attackers do
Protected Backup Vault — stores clean backups the attacker can't reach
